results.title: excellent
results.text: Visit and Darshan to Pashupatinath was great experience. More cleanliness should be observed. Details of temple should also be put at various places. Security should also be tightened.

results.title: Worth a visit!
results.text: I book this tour and did tour with Sumit. A very friendly guide who speaks English, sharing the history of Pashupatinath. This place is very much a part of the Nepali community, and you'll enjoy the narration from the guide. I highly recommend you to book the tour to understand the place better.

results.title: An eye opening. wonderful culture
results.text: I was with Mr Sumit a young Nepali guy with good spoken English. He shows me around and educated me about the culture. It was an eye opening and a mixed feeling on the Hindu culture and the process of cremanation. This experience humbling me in so many ways.. i have the best time in my life.. i became a better person than i am before.  A must place to visit when u are in Nepal and dont forget look for Mr Sumit. He will not dissapoint you. Surely u will enjoy his company just as much as i do.. (:

results.title: Nearly "overwhelming"
results.text: Depending upon when you visit, you can experience so much, not  just the "Place", it's architecture and it's Heritage, but as a truly visceral  experience into the culture of this remarkable city, it's inhabitants, their religions and customs. Come on the right days during festivals, and the colours will amaze you with all the beautiful women dressed in their finest colours. Pilgrims come to pray at the Temple. Families performing the last rights and Cremation ceremonies . It all happens here, at Pashupati Nath. A visit to Pashupatinath on Monday. Every Monday in the Nepali month of July ( by the Nepali Calandar) is celebrated especially by the Hindu women, who dress in their brightest clothing, mostly red, adorned with plastic bangles on their arms, getting Henna applied. Here to go to Temple and pray for long lives for their husbands. Pashupatinath is also home to the cities main Cremation site. Tho's families with enough money witll cremate their loved ones on a traditional wood fire. there is an electric Crematorium close by for those that cannot afford the more traditional ceremony. Loved ones feet are lowered and dipped into the holy Bagmatti River one last time, sprinkled with the holy water, adorned with fresh flowers and then placed upon the traditionally arranged stacks of wood. If you are a tourist here, please respect the families and what they are going through, you are a guest in their private moment. Stay across the river , take photos with discretion, and respect. While it may seem like a tourist attraction, it is real life. This is also a very large Temple area, there is an adjacent Deer park, and you can walk completely around this place in about 1 hours time. many many steps if you want to circumnavigate the entire place. There are also many "Holy"?? men, in various places, they seem to situate themselves in conspicuous places closest to where the tourists are. They are 99 % Naked, covered in grey ash. Yes, you can take pictures if you pay! Why else are they there???  Still interesting, and free to look. There are a dozen ways into the Temple grounds, go with a guide, and they will take you through the main gate so they get a cut of your admission fee (very pricy for Nepal, I think 1000 Rupees depending upon what day and how greedy they are at that moment. Don't pay it, go around, find your own way in, they are just pocketing the money. This is free to everyone, else except tourists, so ignore them if you can, keep walking, say you are on pilgrimage, whatever... and of course, you can always pay. But... that still won't get you entry into the Temple itself. Want access, ??? you must be Hindu, at least for the day, yes it can be done, just go it alone, not as a large group if you really want full access to this incredible place. Also, if you come, get change from one of the change people just outside, they will give you a handful of 5 and 10 rupee bills to leave at all the many important sites, where if you want to wax Hindu you must leave an offering.

results.title: Pashupatinanth Temple
results.text: One of the beautiful temple I have come across. Don't miss the evening aarti. You can the dead bodies being cremated at the banks of the river bagmati at the bottom.

results.title: Divinity
results.text:
Jay Shambho! 
Must visit for realization of reality of life and transformation. 
At the same time visiting Kirateshwor Mahadev Temple, Cosmic Temple, and Guheshwori Temple is meaningful.

results.title: Holy Visit!
results.text:
I was travelling with my wife and the purpose of my trip to Nepal was to visit the Pashupatinath Temple. We could visit the temple twice in two days. Booked for a Puja which was performed at 9.00 in the morning. We had darshan from all gates.
This is a major pilgrimage site for Hindus. It was a beautiful experience. 
The duration there was done very smoothly unlike you do at any Shiva temples in India. Credit goes to the team who does the temple management. People are very cooperative.

results.title: The greatest lord in the world for Hinduism.
results.text:
Pashupati Nath Temple is the heart of all Hinduism situated in Kathmandu, capital city of Nepal, 

Every year millions and millions people visit there from around the world to get peace.

results.title: Visit once in a lifetime
results.text: Pashupatinath temple is Hindus temple located in Kathmandu valley and it is worth to visit once you are in Kathmandu.

results.title: Siva temple with a difference
results.text: Very unique temple where the offerings are in the form of Rudraksha. No one ask money here. River Bagmati flows abutting the temple. The Shiva Linga has four faces at four sides and one face on the top of Linga. So, totally it is five faced and very different. Better to plan in advance for Abhisekham by registering a ticket of NPR 1100/

results.title: A life time wish accomplished
results.text: Cool, easy to visit though it is always crowded. Spent a couple of hours in the temple with my wife. Had a good time duly helped by a local

results.title: Soul satisfaction
results.text: The temple visit gives the satisfaction of visiting one of the most  holy places of  Hinduism. The temple premises is also well maintained.

results.title: Awesome place
results.text:
I really love the Pashupatinath-Temple. It's great to see other methods of saying farewell to the loved ones.

But the business is hard around here. Several guides, sellers, and so on will annoy you.

results.title: In the Lap of Lord Shiva
results.text: It is one of the most famous temples of the world. Quiet and peaceful. You will find many other temples within this temple. If you can... visit early morning during 8:30-9:30 as you will be able to see the morning puja....you will love it. The entire process is breathtaking and it also gives you positive vibes.

results.title: Holy Place
results.text:
One of the main and most famous temples in Nepal. The temple outer area was little destroyed because of the earthquake but inside everything is as it is. It is the most important temple dedicated to god Shiva. One of the most astonishing decorations of the temple is the huge golden statue of Nandi - Shiva’s bull.
A must place to visit if in Nepal.

results.title: Nice architect work.
results.text: One of the main temple of Nepal. At present the temple outer area was bit detsroyed due to the earthquake tht took place laat year. One should defintly go and worship.

results.title: Must Vist
results.text: The inner sanctum is only for Hindus, but, everyone can visit the rest of the facilities. it is clean and has some really old architecture structures.

results.title: Worthy but very expensive
results.text: We paid a lot for a visit to this place. Cremations are a different experience but we were not able to see any temple inside. I think the fee should be lower

results.title: Beautiful and Strange
results.text: Coming from an American perspective, it was so strange to me to see open funeral ceremonies and cremations. But it was definitely an interesting experience. The temple is for Hindu only, but looks beautiful from the outside. We spent about an hour walking around the area, and actually saw a family mourning over a lost loved one. It's emotional, and a bit heavy, but definitely cool to experience that aspect of another culture.

results.title: Pashupatinath temple is listed on world heritage site.It is a religious temple of Hinduism.
results.text:
Pashupatinath is also one of the richest temples in Nepal, having received a great deal of wealth from kings and aristocrats in devotion to the god. The temple buildings are unfortunately closed to non-Hindu visitors, but the site can be enjoyed by all and it makes for a fascinating visit.
We can find many morals and knowledge of life through visiting Pashupatinath temple
